Date: 2025-11-15 09:02 -0800
Subject: Mid‑month capacity smoothing & one‑time true‑up amendment request

Jared —

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. Per our conversation, BrightLane is expecting a short, high‑volume window for the holiday test that will exceed your committed headroom for ~36 hours (predicted peak Nov 20‑21). To avoid service friction, we want to propose a one‑time, provisional quota increase + a temporary reduced overrun rate for that window and a small pro‑rata true‑up rather than full monthly overage billing.

Attached: a first‑pass amendment with the numbers we discussed and the usage extract I pulled (usage-report-Nov1-14.csv). Key asks from our side:
- Confirm you can accept a provisional +30% qps uplift for Nov 20 00:00–Nov 21 12:00 PT.
- We propose capping your overrun rate for that window at $0.045/token equivalent (vs standard $0.075) and applying a single pro‑rata invoice true‑up for the incremental tokens consumed.
- If you want legal changes, we can push a short addendum. Otherwise we can do a billing memo.

Ben — looping you and Lauren for pricing/legal signoff on the reduced overrun tier and the invoicing language.

Next step: Jared, if that alignment looks good I can send an amendment (DocuSign or be a billing memo) by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Logan

—
Logan Wright
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555‑0123

Logan —

Appreciate the proactive heads up and the draft. The temporary uplift makes sense for our run‑of‑test; procurement wants one small change: rather than a reduced overrun rate for the window, they prefer a capped spend commitment for that 36‑hour period (they want predictability on the invoice). If we can agree to a capped incremental spend number (say $25k incremental cap for the window), procurement will sign faster.

Also — we need the amendment to include a short clause that the uplift does not change data retention or access. Procurement: procurement@brightlane.io is on Cc for legal review.

Can you send a version that swaps the reduced per‑token rate for a capped spend, and include the short data/access clause?

Thanks,
Jared

jared.k@brightlane.io

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-15 14:06 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid‑month capacity smoothing & one‑time true‑up amendment request

Logan / Lauren —

Quick notes from pricing/legal:
1) Capped incremental spend for a defined window is fine operationally; we'll translate that to a soft throttle if reached and generate an itemized true‑up entry on the next invoice.
2) Suggest a small non‑recurring setup fee ($350) to cover priority routing + temporary capacity reservation — keeps customers from gaming the cap repeatedly.
3) Include the data/access clause Jared requested as a one‑liner: "This temporary uplift does not modify data retention, access, or audit obligations as described in the Master Services Agreement."

Lauren — can you draft the short amendment language and a DocuSign-ready redline? I can approve the pricing as: +30% qps provisional uplift (Nov 20 00:00–Nov 21 12:00 PT), cap incremental spend at $25,000, $350 one‑time setup fee. If legal ok, Logan can send to BrightLane for signature.

—Ben

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-16 09:24 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid‑month capacity smoothing & one‑time true‑up amendment request

All —

Drafted amendment attached (BL-3472_proposed_amendment_v1.pdf). Highlights:
- Section 1: Temporary Capacity Increase — +30% qps for the exact UTC window (2025‑11‑20T08:00Z to 2025‑11‑21T20:00Z).
- Section 2: Financials — capped incremental spend: $25,000; one‑time setup fee: $350; any consumption beyond cap will be billed at standard overrun rates.
- Section 3: No change to data retention, access, or audit rights.
- Execution: DocuSign recommended; billing memo accepted if procurement signs via email and references the Doc ID.

I left a single comment for legal on the fallback behavior once the cap is hit — we need to be explicit whether we throttle or continue at standard rates and invoice the overage. Ben, per your note, we propose to throttle to preserve platform stability and mark throttled minutes in the usage file.

If everyone signs off I will prepare the DocuSign package and include the usage-report as an annex for reconciliation.

—Lauren
